processing: Orthodox Ceylon black tea in grades such as OP, OPA and FBOP, made in the estate's own factory.
harvest_season: Little is published on a best season for this estate; as elsewhere in Uva, it is picked through the year with dry-weather lots usually most valued.
appearance_dry: Long, dark, wiry leaf in OP and OPA, and smaller leaf in FBOP.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, as with mid-grown Uva teas.
taste_profile: Little is recorded in detail; expect a medium-bodied, rounded Ceylon black tea, typical of mid-elevation Uva, with OP grades smoother than the small broken ones.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western style. The long OP leaf opens slowly, so allow an extra half minute or so.

vintage_note: Sold through the Colombo auction by grade, without a vintage, and exclusively brokered by Forbes & Walker. Retail packs are single-estate OP or similar of recent production; drink them within a year or two.
description:
Shawlands is a mid-elevation estate at Lunugala in the Passara district of Uva, between about 792 and 1,173 metres and covering roughly 515 hectares. It is managed by Hapugastenna Plantations, and it is a name the auction room knows better than the tea shelf.

The tea is orthodox black, made in its own factory, and long-leaf grades such as OP and OPA have been its most notable performers at auction. The Sri Lanka Tea Board has also given it a two-star rating for its practices, and an FBOP won one star at the Great Taste Awards 2022.

Brew OP with a little more time than you would give a broken grade, since the long leaf opens slowly. It suits drinking plain, while FBOP stands up better to milk.

Be careful with listings: a Shawlands Tea Estate near Nuwara Eliya also appears online with different details, and it may not be the same place. Look for Lunugala or Uva on the pack.
history:
The estate's origins are placed in the early 1880s, with 1880 itself given by one account. The factory was built in the late 1930s and has been renovated several times since.

Its recent reputation comes from the Colombo auction: repeated record prices, including Rs. 2,150 per kilo for an OP/OPA in 2022.
